title: Kingdom of Benin
summary: The Kingdom of Benin, in what is now Nigeria, took shape as a state in the 13th century, with Benin City as royal capital. It reached its greatest extent under Oba Ewuare (r. 1440-1473) and traded with the Portuguese from the late 15th century. In 1897 a British expedition of about 1,200 troops conquered it; troops removed an estimated 3,000-5,000 objects.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia says "13th century" in its text and c. 1100 in its timeline; end is the 1897 British conquest.

as_recorded.value: Formed in the 13th century CE as a state proper
1897: a "punitive expedition" of about 1,200 troops was sent to Benin City

where.historical_name: Benin City, capital of the Kingdom of Benin (Edo Kingdom)

importance.justification: Major West African kingdom known for its court brass art and for the 1897 conquest and looting.

audience_note: Covers a colonial military conquest and the removal of thousands of royal objects after an ambush that killed seven British officials and most of their African servants and porters. The museum source calls the term "Benin Bronzes" misleading because the objects include brass, ivory and wood; most objects are now in European and North American museums.
reviewer_note: Least sure of the founding date (13th century versus c. 1100 on the same page). Looting figures are an estimate ("3,000 to 5,000 objects"). The slave-trade link is loose: the pages say Benin banned the sale of male slaves in 1516.
